display.purpose: The name only, inside the wide hero axes, sized to the panel with container units.

lede.purpose: The single research statement under the hero, 34ch.

title.purpose: Entry headings and the Updates heading.

body.purpose: All reading text at a 68ch measure, old-style proportional figures.

caption.purpose: Figure captions, profile links, slider row; DejaVu Sans.

tick.purpose: Axis tick values in label gray.

motion.name: ease-state

components.css: .ds-ref { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 3rem minmax(0, 1fr); padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem; font: 400 1.1875rem/1.55 "STIX Two Text", serif; color: #121212; transition: background-color 600ms ease-out; } .ds-ref:hover { background: #e9f2f9; } .ds-ref p { margin: 0; } .ds-ref__n { padding-top: 0.25rem; color: #616161; font: 400 0.875rem "DejaVu Sans", Verdana, sans-serif; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums lining-nums; } .ds-ref__title { font-weight: 700; line-height: 1.35; } .ds-ref__title a { color: #121212; text-decoration-thickness: 1px; text-underline-offset: 0.2em; text-decoration-color: #e3e3e3; } .ds-ref__title a:hover { color: #12507d; text-decoration-color: currentColor; } .ds-ref__title a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #1f77b4; outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-ref__meta { margin-top: 0.25rem; color: #404040; } .ds-ref__meta strong { color: #121212; }

narrative.overview:
The page is laid out the way a machine-learning paper presents results: a white figure ground, imshow panels framed by thin black spines with outward ticks, numbered figure captions, and bracketed [n] citations that jump to a reference list. Every visual device is borrowed from matplotlib and the publication page, never from web-template furniture. The only material is grayscale Gaussian noise, i.i.d. standard-normal samples painted one per pixel on a canvas and scaled up with crisp, pixelated edges.

Two voices carry the type: STIX Two Text, a scientific serif, for the name, headings and reading text; DejaVu Sans, matplotlib's default label face, for everything a plot would label (ticks, captions, dates, navigation, buttons, reference numbers). Color is almost absent. The matplotlib default cycle supplies the only two hues: tab:blue for links and focus, tab:orange for the one live marker. Density is generous and editorial: long section gaps, a 68ch measure, and no containers around content.

Motion is one authored moment. On load the hero samples from t = 1 to t = 0, the name and portrait resolving out of noise, and the t slider lets the visitor re-noise both panels. Nothing else on the page animates in.
keyCharacteristics: White ground, near-black ink, three gray steps for text hierarchy.
1px black spines with 5px outward ticks frame every image and the time axis of dated entries.
Pixelated N(0,1) grayscale noise as the single material.
tab:blue links; tab:orange on the slider handle only.
Square corners everywhere; no shadows, gradients or cards.
Serif for reading, DejaVu Sans for anything a plot would label.

rules.name: The One Orange Rule
rules.body: Tab orange appears on exactly one element: the handle of the live t slider. Bullets, highlights and badges stay in ink or tab blue.

rules.name: The Matplotlib Cycle Rule
rules.body: New hues come from the matplotlib default cycle in its order, and only for a plotted or interactive mark. Nothing is decorated with color.

rules.name: The Plot Label Rule
rules.body: If matplotlib would draw it as a label (ticks, axis titles, captions, dates, numbers in brackets, controls), it is DejaVu Sans with tabular lining figures. Everything a reader reads as prose is STIX.

rules.name: The Math Italic Rule
rules.body: Variables in captions and axis titles (t, x, ε, N) are STIX italic at about 1.12 to 1.15em, even inside DejaVu text.

rules.name: The Figure Is Flat Rule
rules.body: A surface that needs separation gets a 1px spine or hairline, never a shadow or a tinted card.

dos: Do frame every image or figure as axes: 1px ink spine, 5px outward ticks, DejaVu tick labels, and a "Figure n." caption.
Do use the noise field, with real N(0,1) samples at the panel's own pixel grid, as the placeholder for missing imagery.
Do cite claims with bracketed [n] numbers that link to the reference list.
Do keep tab orange on the slider handle alone, and links in tab blue (#1f77b4).
Do keep every corner square (0px) and every rule 1px.
Do give any new motion a reduced-motion state that shows the settled result.
donts: Don't add cards, tinted panels, shadows, gradients or rounded tiles; separation is a spine or a hairline.
Don't use tab orange for text, bullets or highlights.
Don't set prose in DejaVu or labels in STIX; the split follows the Plot Label Rule.
Don't add entrance animations beyond the hero sampling run.
Don't use colored or smoothed noise; it is grayscale and pixelated.
